```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## Evaluation inputs

Assess the final released data, not an obsolete reconstruction. Keep the cleaned
training reference, categorical target, saved discretizers, selected pairs and
conditioning variable with each release. The real nonmember holdout must not
have been used in generation or guide fitting. The calls below are templates
for existing objects; they are not executed while building this vignette.

```{r fidelity-template}
# result: a completed spades_synthesise() result
fidelity <- SPADES.IND::spades_fidelity_audit(
  reference = result$prepared$data,
  categorical = result$categorical,
  released = result$data,
  reference_values = result$prepared$original,
  discretizers = result$prepared$numeric_discretizers,
  pairs = result$landing$pairs,
  conditional_on = result$landing$conditional_on)
```

## Reconstruction and fidelity checks

Always evaluate the final release as well as its categorical representation.
Reapplying the saved discretizers must recover every selected bin. The package
rejects bin crossings. Categorical fidelity is therefore invariant under valid
reconstruction, but numerical distributions must still be assessed separately.
Use `spades_fidelity_audit()` with the saved pairs, conditioning variable,
discretizers, categorical target and final numerical release. It reports marginal,
bivariate and conditional components, along with numerical distribution checks.
Do not infer full joint-distribution fidelity from small selected-component errors.

## Privacy and membership inference

`spades_privacy_audit()` uses the actual final release, training members and real
nonmembers. It reports duplicates and exact matches and evaluates distance,
density, nearest-neighbour and RF attacks. Candidate profiles shared between
member and nonmember groups are excluded; candidate classes are balanced.
Attack training, calibration and test partitions are separate. Calibration sets
select thresholds and attacks; held-out attack test sets measure performance.
Controls include permuted membership labels and a hypothetical copied release.

`spades_mia_stability()` repeats attack partitions on the same cached release and
candidate features. Repeated splits overlap, so their variability is descriptive,
not independent replication. Near-chance attack performance is limited empirical
evidence for the tested attacks, not a privacy certificate. Candidate-source
mismatch can confound the results. Audit outputs may contain record-level links;
choose an explicit output directory outside the package source.

## Stability and external predictive utility

Fixed-pool target stability repeats landing and reconstruction with different
target seeds while preserving the pool and guide. It does not measure flight
variability. For external utility use `spades_external_utility()` with a named
list of final synthetic targets, the cleaned real training data and the same
untouched real holdout. Use one fixed model seed and the same hyperparameters
across targets. Ten targets with XT, bootstrap CART and XGB entail thirty synthetic
fits plus three real baselines; no model-seed grid is required.

Classification reports accuracy and probabilistic metrics; regression reports
RMSE, MAE and R-squared. Guide performance used by landing is not a substitute
for this external assessment. Shared-holdout comparisons and repeated targets
are dependent. Cache-compatible completed external fits can be reused.

## Membership audit template

Use matching columns and complete member/nonmember data. The audit requires at
least 200 eligible distinct profiles per membership class after exclusions;
the tiny workflow examples are intentionally too small for this analysis.

```{r membership-template}
privacy <- SPADES.IND::spades_privacy_audit(
  members = result$prepared$original,
  nonmembers = real_holdout,
  released = result$data,
  out_dir = file.path(audit_directory, "privacy"),
  seeds = 20261100L + seq_len(20L), threads = 6L)
```

## External utility template

A named list permits comparison of multiple final targets. Keep the model seed
fixed across the list so that varying the target is the intended experimental
factor. Use `mode="regression"` for a numerical response. This is distinct from
optimizing the fixed guide during landing.

```{r external-template}
utility <- SPADES.IND::spades_external_utility(
  reference = real_training,
  synthetic = released_targets,
  holdout = real_holdout,
  target = response_name,
  mode = "classification",
  models = c("XT", "Bagging_CART", "XGB"),
  seed = 20261026L, threads = 6L,
  out_dir = file.path(audit_directory, "external_utility"))
```

## Reporting results

Report the number of cleaned training rows and excluded rows, target and pool
sizes, fidelity components rather than only their mean, numerical reconstruction
checks, duplicates, exact matches and MIA attack performance with controls.
For multiple targets report the range and variability across targets, and retain
per-target results. Report probabilistic classification metrics as well as
accuracy. Distinguish uncertainty across targets from uncertainty across model
seeds; the fixed-seed protocol does not estimate the latter.

Keep protocol settings, software versions, seeds and cached result provenance.
Do not describe an incomplete or interrupted analysis as a completed evaluation.
Near-chance membership attacks do not rule out untested attacks. Improved
accuracy does not imply improved probabilistic predictions or full fidelity.
